items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Kenny has been wanting to produce a record for me... I did some recording over there... Kenny as I said, Kenny was -- it was his date

ctx.x: Well yes. He didn't -- wasn't a regular student, you know, but as I say I enjoy doing this, you know. As you know I'm very hung up on chordal structure and progressions, and different voicings, and when I hear someone play I'm on pins and needles because so much they leave out. And I'll give you an example. We were at a party, Kenny and I, and Kenny played a tune for me and he played a very -- beautifully. But there were so many ways he could have gone that he left out and he asked me play it for him, you know,…

But any way I sat down and I played it for him just to show him how many ways to go, and the different voicing. But this is because I'm just -- this has just been my thing. You know. So now I'm beginning to write a few things for guitar, and just to show, you know, show them how to voice. And different progressions and directions to take. You know because it's hard to -- and because I think this is an --
